claims.reason: Backed: each concept taken separately (Ograniczenia#1: the Android help page ties permissions to device functions; RODO Art. 4 pkt 11 defines consent). Not backed: the instruction to keep the two apart, that is, that an app permission is not itself a consent. No cited source relates one to the other (Ograniczenia#2 says so itself), and recital 32 of the RODO snapshot (lines 369-370) says that choosing technical settings can express consent where the context clearly shows acceptance. I looked in both snapshots for any text that links system permissions with consent and found none.

claims.reason: Read Art. 7 ust. 1 to 4 in full (lines 2496-2513). Ust. 4 only names the dependence of a contract or service on consent as a factor to be taken into account to the greatest extent; it states no rule on when a service has to stay available after a refusal. Related but non-operative text exists: recital 43 (lines 512-518) says consent is not regarded as voluntary if performance of a contract is made dependent on a consent that is not necessary for it. It also does not say when the service must remain available.

scope_gaps.note: The title asserts that the two must be kept apart. The sources define each notion but never relate them, and recital 32 allows technical settings to count as consent in context.

The snapshot is the original Official Journal text of 4.5.2016, not a consolidated version; later corrections were not checked. The duty is addressed to the controller (art. 5 ust. 2, line 2407), which the sentence does not name.
The page is only an Android help page; the sentence's '(Google)' attribution is not in the page text. Also, line 115 of the page says it may contain AI-translated text that can contain errors.
'Uprawnienie systemowe' is stated generally, but the only source is the Android help page; other systems (for example iOS) are not covered.

Statement about the sources as a whole. Recital 32 is non-operative text but addresses when a technical setting can express consent. Absence on the Android side is only from the stored main article region.
Applies to Art. 7 ust. 4 only. Recital 43 gives a stronger statement (consent not regarded as voluntary when the contract depends on unnecessary consent) that the item does not cite.

The Android page describes the permission prompt and where to change permissions; it does not itself advise reading purposes or declining bulk acceptance. The advice is the editors' use of those facts.

The clause 'część funkcji może przestać działać' is treated as the editors' cost estimate. The Android page only says that a refused permission cannot be used by the app (line 37); it does not say which features stop working.

notes: Opened only: pl-source-verifier.md, AGENTS.md, the packet, and the two listed snapshots 89be0046cf8ac2b2.txt (RODO, Official Journal of 4.5.2016, whole text) and 96ed8430ad13bbdc.txt (Android help page, article region only). No protocol violation. Judgement calls: (1) the '(Google)' attribution in Korzyść i dowody#4 is not in the text between the snapshot markers, so the row is partly; (2) title#1 is partly because no source relates permissions to consent; (3) Ograniczenia#2.2 is partly because of recital 32; (4) the short article headings 'Artykuł 4' and 'Artykuł 7' are quoted with cell:true although they are headings, not table cells, to evidence the numbers 4 and 7 in the claims; (5) Ocena dowodów#1 was split into a source_description and an absence claim, and the grade letter C was not checked. The Android page notes that its Polish text may be AI-translated and may contain errors (line 115).
